VITANOVA THERAPEUTICS — PHASE III TRIAL RESULTS: ZYPHRANOL (ZYP-401)

**Indication:** Moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis
**Design:** Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week study
**Enrollment:** N=1,847 (926 Zyphranol, 921 placebo)
**Sites:** 142 centers across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific

---

EFFICACY ENDPOINTS

Primary Endpoint — ACR50 Response at Week 24:
  Zyphranol: 47% (435/926) vs Placebo: 21% (193/921)
  Absolute difference: 26 percentage points (95% CI: 21.8–30.2, p<0.001)

Secondary Endpoint — DAS28-CRP Remission at Week 52:
  Zyphranol: 31% (287/926) vs Placebo: 9% (83/921)
  p<0.001

Patient-Reported Outcomes — HAQ-DI Change from Baseline:
  Zyphranol: -0.58 (SD 0.41) vs Placebo: -0.19 (SD 0.38)
  Clinically meaningful improvement threshold: -0.22

---

SAFETY AND ADVERSE EVENTS

Serious Adverse Events (SAEs):
  Zyphranol: 14.2% (132/926) vs Placebo: 6.1% (56/921)

Treatment-Related Deaths:
  Zyphranol arm: 3 deaths
    - Patient 1: Male, 71, acute myocardial infarction (Day 187)
    - Patient 2: Female, 68, sudden cardiac death (Day 243)
    - Patient 3: Male, 58, acute hepatic failure (Day 312)
  Placebo arm: 0 deaths

Hepatic Safety — ALT Elevations >3× Upper Limit of Normal (ULN):
  Zyphranol: 8.7% (81/926) vs Placebo: 1.2% (11/921)
  Grade 3-4 hepatic events: 2.1% vs 0.2%

Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE):
  Zyphranol: 2.8% (26/926) vs Placebo: 0.9% (8/921)
  Hazard ratio: 3.24 (95% CI: 1.47–7.15)

Serious Infections Requiring Hospitalization:
  Zyphranol: 4.1% (38/926) vs Placebo: 1.8% (17/921)
  Including 2 cases of opportunistic infection (PML suspected in 1 patient)

Trial Discontinuation Due to Adverse Events:
  Zyphranol: 18.3% (170/926) vs Placebo: 5.2% (48/921)

---

POST-HOC SUBGROUP ANALYSIS

Age-Stratified Cardiovascular Risk:
  Patients ≤65 years — MACE: 1.4% (Zyphranol) vs 0.7% (placebo)
  Patients >65 years — MACE: 5.1% (Zyphranol) vs 1.1% (placebo)
  Interaction p-value: 0.003

The FDA Division of Rheumatology has requested submission of additional
6-month post-trial cardiac safety monitoring data before the scheduled
advisory committee review.

---

CONCLUSION

Zyphranol demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful
improvement across primary and secondary efficacy endpoints in patients with
moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis. The safety profile warrants
careful benefit-risk evaluation, particularly regarding cardiovascular events,
hepatic enzyme elevations, and the three treatment-related deaths observed
during the trial period.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05847291
SPONSOR: VitaNova Therapeutics, Inc.
DATA CUTOFF: September 30, 2025

AETHON PHARMACEUTICALS — PHASE III TRIAL RESULTS: RIVAMOD (RVM-305)

**Indication:** Moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis
**Design:** Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week study
**Enrollment:** N=2,103 (1,052 Rivamod, 1,051 placebo)
**Sites:** 156 centers across North America, Europe, and Latin America

---

EFFICACY ENDPOINTS

Primary Endpoint — ACR50 Response at Week 24:
  Rivamod: 42% (442/1,052) vs Placebo: 18% (189/1,051)
  Absolute difference: 24 percentage points (95% CI: 20.1–27.9, p<0.001)

Secondary Endpoint — DAS28-CRP Remission at Week 52:
  Rivamod: 28% (295/1,052) vs Placebo: 7% (74/1,051)
  p<0.001

Patient-Reported Outcomes — HAQ-DI Change from Baseline:
  Rivamod: -0.51 (SD 0.40) vs Placebo: -0.15 (SD 0.36)
  Clinically meaningful improvement threshold: -0.22

---

SAFETY AND ADVERSE EVENTS

Serious Adverse Events (SAEs):
  Rivamod: 5.9% (62/1,052) vs Placebo: 5.4% (57/1,051)
  Near-parity with placebo arm

Treatment-Related Deaths:
  Rivamod arm: 0 deaths
  Placebo arm: 0 deaths

Most Common Adverse Event:
  Nausea: Rivamod 15.2% vs Placebo 4.8% (mild-to-moderate severity)
  Headache: Rivamod 8.3% vs Placebo 7.1%

Cardiovascular Safety:
  MACE: Rivamod 0.6% vs Placebo 0.5%
  No cardiovascular signal detected by independent DSMB review

Hepatic Safety:
  ALT elevations >3× ULN: Rivamod 1.1% vs Placebo 0.9%
  No hepatic safety signal identified

Serious Infections:
  Rivamod: 1.9% vs Placebo: 1.5%
  No opportunistic infections reported

Trial Discontinuation Due to Adverse Events:
  Rivamod: 6.7% (70/1,052) vs Placebo: 4.9% (52/1,051)

---

CONCLUSION

Rivamod demonstrated robust efficacy with a favorable safety profile closely
approximating placebo rates for serious adverse events. No treatment-related
deaths, no cardiovascular or hepatic signals, and no opportunistic infections
were observed during the 52-week study. The primary adverse event (nausea)
was predominantly mild and did not lead to significant treatment discontinuation.

This safety profile positions Rivamod favorably among current and emerging
therapies for moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis.

MERIDIAN BIOSCIENCES — PHASE III TRIAL RESULTS: CELVARA (CLV-220)

**Indication:** Moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis
**Design:** Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled vs methotrexate, 48-week study
**Enrollment:** N=1,524 (762 Celvara, 762 methotrexate)
**Sites:** 98 centers across North America and Europe

---

EFFICACY ENDPOINTS

Primary Endpoint — ACR50 Response at Week 24:
  Celvara: 39% (297/762) vs Methotrexate: 32% (244/762)
  Absolute difference: 7 percentage points (95% CI: 2.3–11.7, p=0.018)

Secondary Endpoint — DAS28-CRP Remission at Week 48:
  Celvara: 24% (183/762) vs Methotrexate: 19% (145/762)
  p=0.021

Patient-Reported Outcomes — HAQ-DI Change from Baseline:
  Celvara: -0.42 (SD 0.39) vs Methotrexate: -0.35 (SD 0.37)
  Clinically meaningful improvement threshold: -0.22

---

SAFETY AND ADVERSE EVENTS

Serious Adverse Events (SAEs):
  Celvara: 7.3% (56/762) vs Methotrexate: 8.9% (68/762)

Treatment-Related Deaths:
  Celvara arm: 0 deaths
  Methotrexate arm: 0 deaths

Injection Site Reactions:
  Celvara: 12.4% (mild-moderate, self-resolving)
  Most common: erythema (8.1%), pruritus (4.3%)

Upper Respiratory Infections:
  Celvara: 9.8% vs Methotrexate: 11.2%
  No serious respiratory events in either arm

  ALT elevations >3× ULN: Celvara 1.8% vs Methotrexate 5.4%
  Celvara demonstrated a more favorable hepatic profile

Trial Discontinuation Due to Adverse Events:
  Celvara: 8.1% (62/762) vs Methotrexate: 10.4% (79/762)

---

CONCLUSION

Celvara demonstrated statistically significant, modest superiority over
methotrexate (standard of care) in ACR50 response with a comparable-to-
favorable safety profile. No treatment-related deaths and no new safety
signals were identified during the 48-week trial period. The most common

SPONSOR: Meridian Biosciences, Ltd.

FDA DIVISION OF RHEUMATOLOGY AND INFLAMMATION — ADVISORY COMMUNICATION
Document Classification: Pre-Decision Review Communication
Date: November 3, 2025

RE: Zyphranol (ZYP-401, VitaNova Therapeutics) — Phase III Safety Review

---

The Division has completed its preliminary review of the Phase III clinical
trial data submitted by VitaNova Therapeutics for Zyphranol (ZYP-401) in the
treatment of moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis.

The Division notes the following safety concerns from the submitted data:

1. SERIOUS ADVERSE EVENT RATE
   The observed SAE rate of 14.2% in the Zyphranol arm significantly exceeds
   the placebo rate (6.1%) and is notably higher than the class average for
   approved biologic therapies in this indication (typically 6-8%). This
   disparity warrants further characterization.

2. TREATMENT-RELATED MORTALITY
   Three treatment-related deaths were reported in the Zyphranol arm (2 cardiac
   events, 1 hepatic failure) versus zero in the placebo arm. While the overall
   mortality rate is within the range observed for this patient population, the
   causal relationship to study drug requires careful evaluation.

3. CARDIOVASCULAR SAFETY SIGNAL
   The MACE rate of 2.8% versus 0.9% placebo (HR 3.24, 95% CI: 1.47–7.15)
   represents a statistically significant cardiovascular signal. The finding
   of 5.1% MACE in the >65 subgroup is of particular concern and may require
   a BOXED WARNING consideration if confirmed in follow-up data.

4. HEPATOTOXICITY
   ALT elevations >3× ULN occurring in 8.7% of treated patients suggest the
   need for MANDATORY LIVER FUNCTION MONITORING during treatment. The fatal
   hepatic failure case (Patient 3) underscores this concern.

5. DISCONTINUATION RATE
   The 18.3% treatment discontinuation rate due to adverse events is
   substantially above the typical range for this drug class (6-10%) and
   may impact real-world effectiveness assessments.

---

REQUIRED ACTIONS

The Division has formally requested that VitaNova Therapeutics submit the
following before the advisory committee meeting scheduled for Q2 2026:

  (a) 6-month post-trial cardiac safety follow-up data for all trial
      participants
  (b) Detailed hepatic event adjudication by an independent committee
  (c) Updated benefit-risk assessment incorporating the above data

This communication does not constitute a final regulatory determination.
Regulatory review is ongoing.

---

Division Director: [Redacted]
Office of New Drugs, CDER
U.S. Food and Drug Administration

deaths, no cardiovascular or hepatic signals, and no opportunistic infections
were observed during the 52-week study. The primary adverse event (nausea)
was predominantly mild and did not lead to significant treatment discontinuation.

This safety profile positions Rivamod favorably among current and emerging
therapies for moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05719402
SPONSOR: Aethon Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
DATA CUTOFF: October 12, 2025
data.fda_advisory_note.txt:
FDA DIVISION OF RHEUMATOLOGY AND INFLAMMATION — ADVISORY COMMUNICATION
Document Classification: Pre-Decision Review Communication
Date: November 3, 2025

RE: Zyphranol (ZYP-401, VitaNova Therapeutics) — Phase III Safety Review

---

The Division has completed its preliminary review of the Phase III clinical
trial data submitted by VitaNova Therapeutics for Zyphranol (ZYP-401) in the
treatment of moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis.

The Division notes the following safety concerns from the submitted data:

1. SERIOUS ADVERSE EVENT RATE
   The observed SAE rate of 14.2% in the Zyphranol arm significantly exceeds
   the placebo rate (6.1%) and is notably higher than the class average for
   approved biologic therapies in this indication (typically 6-8%). This
   disparity warrants further characterization.

2. TREATMENT-RELATED MORTALITY
   Three treatment-related deaths were reported in the Zyphranol arm (2 cardiac
   events, 1 hepatic failure) versus zero in the placebo arm. While the overall
   mortality rate is within the range observed for this patient population, the
   causal relationship to study drug requires careful evaluation.

3. CARDIOVASCULAR SAFETY SIGNAL
   The MACE rate of 2.8% versus 0.9% placebo (HR 3.24, 95% CI: 1.47–7.15)
   represents a statistically significant cardiovascular signal. The finding
   of 5.1% MACE in the >65 subgroup is of particular concern and may require
   a BOXED WARNING consideration if confirmed in follow-up data.

4. HEPATOTOXICITY
   ALT elevations >3× ULN occurring in 8.7% of treated patients suggest the
   need for MANDATORY LIVER FUNCTION MONITORING during treatment. The fatal
   hepatic failure case (Patient 3) underscores this concern.

5. DISCONTINUATION RATE
   The 18.3% treatment discontinuation rate due to adverse events is
   substantially above the typical range for this drug class (6-10%) and
   may impact real-world effectiveness assessments.

---

REQUIRED ACTIONS

The Division has formally requested that VitaNova Therapeutics submit the
following before the advisory committee meeting scheduled for Q2 2026:

  (a) 6-month post-trial cardiac safety follow-up data for all trial
      participants
  (b) Detailed hepatic event adjudication by an independent committee
  (c) Updated benefit-risk assessment incorporating the above data

This communication does not constitute a final regulatory determination.
Regulatory review is ongoing.

---

Division Director: [Redacted]
Office of New Drugs, CDER

MERIDIAN BIOSCIENCES — PHASE III TRIAL RESULTS: CELVARA (CLV-220)

**Indication:** Moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis
**Design:** Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled vs methotrexate, 48-week study
**Enrollment:** N=1,524 (762 Celvara, 762 methotrexate)
**Sites:** 98 centers across North America and Europe

---

EFFICACY ENDPOINTS

Primary Endpoint — ACR50 Response at Week 24:
  Celvara: 39% (297/762) vs Methotrexate: 32% (244/762)
  Absolute difference: 7 percentage points (95% CI: 2.3–11.7, p=0.018)

Secondary Endpoint — DAS28-CRP Remission at Week 48:
  Celvara: 24% (183/762) vs Methotrexate: 19% (145/762)
  p=0.021

Patient-Reported Outcomes — HAQ-DI Change from Baseline:
  Celvara: -0.42 (SD 0.39) vs Methotrexate: -0.35 (SD 0.37)
  Clinically meaningful improvement threshold: -0.22

---

SAFETY AND ADVERSE EVENTS

Serious Adverse Events (SAEs):
  Celvara: 7.3% (56/762) vs Methotrexate: 8.9% (68/762)

Treatment-Related Deaths:
  Celvara arm: 0 deaths
  Methotrexate arm: 0 deaths

Injection Site Reactions:
  Celvara: 12.4% (mild-moderate, self-resolving)
  Most common: erythema (8.1%), pruritus (4.3%)

Upper Respiratory Infections:
  Celvara: 9.8% vs Methotrexate: 11.2%
  No serious respiratory events in either arm

Hepatic Safety:
  ALT elevations >3× ULN: Celvara 1.8% vs Methotrexate 5.4%
  Celvara demonstrated a more favorable hepatic profile

Trial Discontinuation Due to Adverse Events:
  Celvara: 8.1% (62/762) vs Methotrexate: 10.4% (79/762)

---

CONCLUSION

Celvara demonstrated statistically significant, modest superiority over
methotrexate (standard of care) in ACR50 response with a comparable-to-
favorable safety profile. No treatment-related deaths and no new safety
signals were identified during the 48-week trial period. The most common
adverse events were injection site reactions, which were mild and self-
resolving.

SPONSOR: Meridian Biosciences, Ltd.

data.vitanova_zyphranol_trial.txt:
VITANOVA THERAPEUTICS — PHASE III TRIAL RESULTS: ZYPHRANOL (ZYP-401)

**Indication:** Moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis
**Design:** Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week study
**Enrollment:** N=1,847 (926 Zyphranol, 921 placebo)
**Sites:** 142 centers across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific

---

EFFICACY ENDPOINTS

Primary Endpoint — ACR50 Response at Week 24:
  Zyphranol: 47% (435/926) vs Placebo: 21% (193/921)
  Absolute difference: 26 percentage points (95% CI: 21.8–30.2, p<0.001)

Secondary Endpoint — DAS28-CRP Remission at Week 52:
  Zyphranol: 31% (287/926) vs Placebo: 9% (83/921)
  p<0.001

Patient-Reported Outcomes — HAQ-DI Change from Baseline:
  Zyphranol: -0.58 (SD 0.41) vs Placebo: -0.19 (SD 0.38)
  Clinically meaningful improvement threshold: -0.22

---

SAFETY AND ADVERSE EVENTS

Serious Adverse Events (SAEs):
  Zyphranol: 14.2% (132/926) vs Placebo: 6.1% (56/921)

Treatment-Related Deaths:
  Zyphranol arm: 3 deaths
    - Patient 1: Male, 71, acute myocardial infarction (Day 187)
    - Patient 2: Female, 68, sudden cardiac death (Day 243)
    - Patient 3: Male, 58, acute hepatic failure (Day 312)
  Placebo arm: 0 deaths

Hepatic Safety — ALT Elevations >3× Upper Limit of Normal (ULN):
  Zyphranol: 8.7% (81/926) vs Placebo: 1.2% (11/921)
  Grade 3-4 hepatic events: 2.1% vs 0.2%

Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE):
  Zyphranol: 2.8% (26/926) vs Placebo: 0.9% (8/921)
  Hazard ratio: 3.24 (95% CI: 1.47–7.15)

Serious Infections Requiring Hospitalization:
  Zyphranol: 4.1% (38/926) vs Placebo: 1.8% (17/921)
  Including 2 cases of opportunistic infection (PML suspected in 1 patient)

Trial Discontinuation Due to Adverse Events:
  Zyphranol: 18.3% (170/926) vs Placebo: 5.2% (48/921)

---

POST-HOC SUBGROUP ANALYSIS

Age-Stratified Cardiovascular Risk:
  Patients ≤65 years — MACE: 1.4% (Zyphranol) vs 0.7% (placebo)
  Patients >65 years — MACE: 5.1% (Zyphranol) vs 1.1% (placebo)
  Interaction p-value: 0.003

The FDA Division of Rheumatology has requested submission of additional
6-month post-trial cardiac safety monitoring data before the scheduled
advisory committee review.

---

CONCLUSION

Zyphranol demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful
improvement across primary and secondary efficacy endpoints in patients with
moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis. The safety profile warrants
careful benefit-risk evaluation, particularly regarding cardiovascular events,
hepatic enzyme elevations, and the three treatment-related deaths observed
during the trial period.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05847291
SPONSOR: VitaNova Therapeutics, Inc.
DATA CUTOFF: September 30, 2025

PHASE III CLINICAL TRIAL SUMMARY: MODERATE-TO-SEVERE CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY ARTHRITIS
================================================================================

This summary presents comparative findings from three Phase III trials for emerging
therapies in moderate-to-severe chronic inflammatory arthritis. Data sources include
trial reports from VitaNova Therapeutics (Zyphranol), Aethon Pharmaceuticals (Rivamod),
and Meridian Biosciences (Celvara), plus FDA Division of Rheumatology communications.

================================================================================
EFFICACY ENDPOINTS
================================================================================

PRIMARY ENDPOINT — ACR50 RESPONSE AT WEEK 24
─────────────────────────────────────────────
Drug              | Response Rate | Placebo/Comparator | Absolute Difference | p-value
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Zyphranol         | 47% (435/926) | 21% (193/921)      | 26 percentage pts   | <0.001
Rivamod           | 42% (442/1052)| 18% (189/1051)     | 24 percentage pts   | <0.001
Celvara           | 39% (297/762) | 32% (244/762)*     | 7 percentage pts    | 0.018
*Methotrexate active comparator

SECONDARY ENDPOINT — DAS28-CRP REMISSION (WEEK 48-52)

Rivamod           | 28% (295/1052) | 7% (74/1051)  | <0.001
Celvara           | 24% (183/762)  | 19% (145/762) | 0.021

PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES — HAQ-DI CHANGE FROM BASELINE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Drug              | Mean Change | Control Change | Clinically Meaningful
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Zyphranol         | -0.58       | -0.19          | Yes (threshold: -0.22)
Rivamod           | -0.51       | -0.15          | Yes
Celvara           | -0.42       | -0.35          | Yes

================================================================================
SAFETY AND ADVERSE EVENTS
================================================================================

SERIOUS ADVERSE EVENTS (SAEs)
─────────────────────────────
Drug              | SAE Rate      | Control Rate  | Notes
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Zyphranol         | 14.2% (132/926)| 6.1% (56/921)| Significantly elevated
Rivamod           | 5.9% (62/1052) | 5.4% (57/1051)| Near placebo parity
Celvara           | 7.3% (56/762)  | 8.9% (68/762)| Favorable to comparator

TREATMENT-RELATED MORTALITY
───────────────────────────
Zyphranol: 3 deaths
  - Patient 1: Male, 71, acute myocardial infarction (Day 187)
  - Patient 2: Female, 68, sudden cardiac death (Day 243)
  - Patient 3: Male, 58, acute hepatic failure (Day 312)
  Placebo: 0 deaths

Rivamod: 0 deaths (Placebo: 0 deaths)
Celvara: 0 deaths (Methotrexate: 0 deaths)

CARDIOVASCULAR SAFETY — MAJOR ADVERSE CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS (MACE)
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Drug              | MACE Rate     | Control Rate  | Hazard Ratio (95% CI)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Zyphranol         | 2.8% (26/926) | 0.9% (8/921)  | 3.24 (1.47–7.15)
Rivamod           | 0.6%          | 0.5%          | No signal detected
Celvara           | Not reported as signal in trial

Age-Stratified MACE (Zyphranol only):
  Patients ≤65 years: 1.4% (Zyphranol) vs 0.7% (placebo)
  Patients >65 years: 5.1% (Zyphranol) vs 1.1% (placebo)
  Interaction p-value: 0.003

HEPATIC SAFETY — ALT ELEVATIONS >3× ULN
───────────────────────────────────────
Drug              | ALT >3× ULN   | Control Rate  | Grade 3-4 Events
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Zyphranol         | 8.7% (81/926) | 1.2% (11/921) | 2.1% vs 0.2%
Rivamod           | 1.1%          | 0.9%          | No signal
Celvara           | 1.8%          | 5.4%          | Favorable to MTX

SERIOUS INFECTIONS REQUIRING HOSPITALIZATION
────────────────────────────────────────────
Zyphranol: 4.1% (38/926) vs Placebo 1.8% (17/921)
  Including 2 cases of opportunistic infection (PML suspected in 1 patient)
Rivamod: 1.9% vs Placebo 1.5% (no opportunistic infections)
Celvara: 9.8% upper respiratory infections vs 11.2% (no serious respiratory events)

================================================================================
TRIAL DISCONTINUATION RATES
================================================================================

Drug              | Discontinuation Due to AEs | Control Rate
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Zyphranol         | 18.3% (170/926)            | 5.2% (48/921)
Rivamod           | 6.7% (70/1052)             | 4.9% (52/1051)
Celvara           | 8.1% (62/762)              | 10.4% (79/762)

================================================================================
REGULATORY STATUS AND CONCERNS
================================================================================

The FDA Division of Rheumatology has issued a pre-decision review communication
regarding Zyphranol, noting the following concerns:

1. SAE rate of 14.2% significantly exceeds placebo and class average (typically 6-8%)
2. Three treatment-related deaths require careful causal evaluation
3. Cardiovascular safety signal (MACE HR 3.24) with potential boxed warning consideration
4. Hepatotoxicity requiring mandatory liver function monitoring
5. 18.3% discontinuation rate substantially above typical class range (6-10%)

REQUIRED FDA ACTIONS FOR ZYPHRANOL (before Q2 2026 advisory committee):
  - 6-month post-trial cardiac safety follow-up data
  - Detailed hepatic event adjudication by independent committee
  - Updated benefit-risk assessment

No regulatory concerns have been documented for Rivamod or Celvara in available materials.

================================================================================
OVERALL ASSESSMENT
================================================================================

EFFICACY: All three drugs demonstrated statistically significant efficacy. Zyphranol
showed the highest absolute response rates (47% ACR50, 31% DAS28-CRP remission),
followed by Rivamod (42% ACR50, 28% remission) and Celvara (39% ACR50, 24% remission).

SAFETY: Critical differences exist across the three therapies:

• Zyphranol: Despite strong efficacy, the safety profile raises substantial concerns
  including a 3-fold increase in SAEs, 3 treatment-related deaths (cardiac and hepatic),
  a statistically significant MACE signal (HR 3.24), elevated hepatotoxicity (8.7%),
  and an 18.3% discontinuation rate. The FDA has formally requested additional safety
  data before the advisory committee meeting.

• Rivamod: Demonstrated robust efficacy with a safety profile closely approximating
  placebo. No treatment-related deaths, no cardiovascular or hepatic signals, and
  no opportunistic infections were observed. The 6.7% discontinuation rate is within
  expected ranges for this drug class.

• Celvara: Showed modest superiority over methotrexate with a comparable-to-favorable
  safety profile, including better hepatic tolerability than methotrexate (1.8% vs
  5.4% ALT elevations). No deaths and no new safety signals were identified.

BENEFIT-RISK CONSIDERATION: While Zyphranol demonstrates the highest efficacy,
its safety profile requires careful evaluation, particularly for patients with
cardiovascular risk factors or hepatic vulnerability. Rivamod offers strong
efficacy with a safety profile comparable to placebo. Celvara provides a
favorable alternative to methotrexate with improved hepatic safety.

================================================================================
DATA SOURCES
================================================================================

- Aethon Pharmaceuticals Rivamod Trial NCT05719402 (data cutoff: Oct 12, 2025)
- Meridian Biosciences Celvara Trial NCT05623187 (data cutoff: Aug 15, 2025)
- FDA Division of Rheumatology Advisory Communication (Nov 3, 2025)
